definition: A specific string or token that, when generated, signals a language model to halt further text generation.
details: Stop sequences are commonly configured in API calls to control output length and formatting, ensuring generation halts at a natural or application-defined boundary rather than continuing indefinitely.

explainer.lead: A specific string or token that, when generated, signals a language model to halt further text generation. It matters for controlling output length and formatting in applications.

tiers.eli5: A word or symbol you tell the model to treat as the finish line, so it stops writing when it gets there.
tiers.practitioner: Configured in API calls to end generation at an application-defined boundary; the pitfall is that if the string never appears, generation continues until another limit applies.
tiers.paperLevel: A configured string or token whose generation halts further text generation, used to ensure output stops at a natural or application-defined boundary rather than continuing indefinitely.

explainer.example: Setting a stop sequence so a generated answer ends at the start of a new section header instead of continuing into it.
